comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 1344 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1344), NOT submitted, ticket left in_progress.

WHERE THE DECISION LIVES, AND WHY. `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities` is DELETED from anthropic_model.py; the decision is now `capabilities.web_search_capabilities(*, web: bool)`. Two reasons for that home: (1) it is no longer an Anthropic construction detail but a capability decision, the same shape as `cache_settings_for(caps, *, execution_mode)` which already lives there; (2) anthropic_model.py's own docstring scopes it to the DIRECT-Anthropic construction path, which this no longer is. The function takes NO model or provider argument at all — web access is required on every provider, so nothing about the provider is an input, and a function handed no model string cannot gate on the shape of one. The runner threads `web_requested = bool(req.web) and not self._model_override` into BOTH the capability call and provenance, so the attached capability and the record that attests it cannot disagree. Renaming was checked with grep for the NAME AS A STRING (not just a symbol search): the only reference was agent_call.py's monkeypatch-hazard docstring, updated; no test monkeypatched the old name.

MECHANISM: one `WebSearch(native=WebSearchTool(max_uses=5), local=duckduckgo_search_tool(max_results=5))`. pydantic-ai keeps the native tool where `profile.supported_native_tools` contains WebSearchTool and drops it for the local tool where it does not — so native is preferred (cheaper, provider-grounded, no third-party text in our process) and local is the floor. NativeOrLocalTool was NOT needed; WebSearch already IS one.

A TRAP WORTH RECORDING. Setting max_uses / blocked_domains / allowed_domains at the CAPABILITY level flips pydantic-ai's `_requires_native()` True, and `NativeOrLocalTool.get_toolset()` then returns None — i.e. the local fallback is SUPPRESSED and the run hard-fails on any provider without the native tool. Hardening the capability the obvious way would have re-created this exact bug. max_uses therefore rides the NATIVE TOOL INSTANCE, where `_requires_native()` does not see it; a test asserts `get_toolset() is not None` so a future edit cannot silently reintroduce that.

SECURITY POSTURE (argued in a block comment above the function, not just here). Fetched content is UNTRUSTED INPUT to a BLOCKING gate. Bounds: VOLUME on both routes (native max_uses=5 per run; local max_results=5 per call; plus the agentic loop's own request/step budget). SHAPE on the local route — pydantic-ai's DuckDuckGo tool returns title+href+snippet ONLY, never page bodies, so this is a SEARCH capability, not the unbounded homegrown HTTP fetch tool the original design was protecting against, and no rebar-side fetcher was written. AUTHORITY downstream — output is validated against the criteria finding contract, and T1's rubric now states results are untrusted data. DOMAIN CONTROLS DELIBERATELY UNUSED, and this is a tradeoff not an omission: an allowlist is self-defeating for a criterion whose job is discovering UNKNOWN prior art, and a blocklist cannot hold uniformly (capability-level kills the fallback per the trap above; native-instance-level binds only one route, and a control that holds on one route and not the other is a misleading control).

OBSERVABILITY: `provider_provenance.capabilities.web_access` is now recorded as "native" | "local" | "off". Three values not a boolean, because the two ON routes are not equivalent (only "local" means third-party text entered rebar's process). `off` wins whenever the run did not attach the capability, so the record can never attest grounding a reviewer did not have. New profile-derived field `ModelCapabilities.native_web_search`, read by MEMBERSHIP in `supported_native_tools` — the same registry pydantic-ai filters against — and intersected with `all()` across a fallback chain.

PACKAGING, PROVEN BY EXECUTION NOT BY READING. `pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,retries,duckduckgo]` — folded into the `agents` extra ITSELF rather than a new opt-in extra, so no deployment can install the agents runtime and forget it; that also means Dockerfile.reviewbot's `uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra reviewbot --extra bedrock` needed NO new flag (a comment there records why, so a future narrowing of `agents` does not silently drop it). uv.lock regenerated and committed (+ddgs 9.14.4, lxml, primp, brotli/brotlicffi, fake-useragent, h2/hpack/hyperframe, socksio). EXECUTED in a venv synced from the new lock: `import pydantic_ai.common_tools.duckduckgo` OK; ddgs 9.14.4; the capability CONSTRUCTS with max_uses=5 and local tool 'duckduckgo_search'; get_native_tools()==['WebSearchTool'] and get_toolset() is not None; web=False -> None. Route read per provider: anthropic/openai/google -> native; bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 -> local (`supported_native_tools` is EMPTY, agreeing with the live Bedrock measurement on this ticket). pip-audit: no known vulnerabilities.

T1 RUBRIC: the hedge is gone ("MAY be offered", "provider-dependent", "when it is not available", "fall back" all removed) and replaced with an assertion that the tool IS available. The anti-fabrication clause is KEPT and strengthened ("cite only sources you actually retrieved"), plus a new clause naming results untrusted data, not instructions.

TESTS — tests/unit/test_web_tool_gating.py rewritten (20 tests), each family verified RED by mutation:
* reinstating the anthropic prefix gate -> 5 RED, including `test_runner_attaches_web_capability_on_every_provider[bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8]` ("web-flagged request on bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 got NO web capability"), the openai and google params, `test_the_decision_takes_no_model_or_provider_input`, and the call-site AST guard ("model/provider passed positionally").
* deleting the provenance field -> RED, `KeyError: 'web_access'`.
* making web=False attach anyway -> 4 RED, `assert 'capabilities' not in unflagged` on all four providers (the no-request path is byte-identical).
* reverting the T1 rubric from git HEAD -> RED, "T1 still frames web access as optional: 'may be offered'"; dropping only the untrusted clause -> RED on that assertion alone.
The attested guard `test_capabilities_module_still_has_no_provider_name_prefix_matching` is untouched and passes; my call-site guard deliberately does not duplicate or weaken it. One pre-existing test updated: test_verdict_provenance.py's exact-dict assertion gained `web_access: off` (with a contradictory native_web_search=True to prove the record does not leak capability as usage).

GATES, all by exit code on a CLEAN tree (`git status --porcelain` empty), re-run after rebasing onto origin/main 5bc3a432d7: make lint 0 · make typecheck 0 · check_comment_hygiene 0 · check_config_reads 0 · check_docs_index 0 · check_raw_git_writes 0 · check_readme_quickstart 0 · check_server_manifest 0 · check_verify_gate_parity 0 · check_wall_clock_asserts 0 · uv lock --check 0 · make config-check 0 · pre-commit run --all-files 0 · pytest -m 'not integration and not external' -n 6 --dist worksteal 0 (9863 passed, 34 skipped).

STILL OPEN, for whoever closes this: acceptance criterion 2 says web access is verified 'by a run on each configured provider, not by inspection of the gate condition'. What I have is the attach path exercised per provider through the runner with the Agent construction captured, plus the route derived from each provider's real profile — no live model call was made on any provider (no spend). A live Bedrock plan-review run showing `web_access: "local"` on a signed verdict would close that criterion outright.

CHANGE 1344 IS UP BUT BLOCKED ON BOTH GATES, AND THE BLOCK IS CHEAP TO CLEAR. Read this before touching the code — the code is probably fine.

https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1344 -- LLM-Review = -1, Verified = -1.

THE LLM-Review BLOCK IS NOT A CODE FINDING. Verbatim: "(bugfix-size-attestation) this change touches 554 non-test line(s) - over the 150-line floor for a bug fix - but bug 129e-2d88-cce2-492c has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record)". So the gate wants a certified plan review on THIS ticket because the fix is large, exactly as the debug protocol warns for a fix whose blast radius reaches non-test code.

AND THE ATTESTATION ALREADY EXISTS - IT IS MERELY STALE. rebar review-plan 129e --status returns verdict "stale-head": signed at 5bc3a432d7 while HEAD has moved on. A plan review was run on this ticket earlier today and returned PASS with 0 blocking. So the first thing to try is rebar sign-review 129e-2d88-cce2-492c, which RE-SIGNS FROM THE RECORDED REVIEW WITH NO LLM SPEND. Only pay for a fresh review-plan if that refuses. Then re-push or comment recheck on 1344.

THE Verified -1 IS UNDIAGNOSED and must not be assumed to be a real test failure. Today's identical-looking failure on another change was the STALE-BASE TRAP: Gerrit CI runs the TARGET branch's workflow against the patchset's tree, so a gate script added to main after the change was based fails on a missing file. 1344 was based on 5bc3a432d7 and main has advanced several times since. CHECK FOR THAT FIRST - rebase onto current origin/main and re-push - before reading the failure as a defect in the change.

WHAT THE CHANGE CONTAINS, per the implementer's report: _anthropic_web_search_capabilities is deleted from anthropic_model.py and replaced by web_search_capabilities(*, web: bool) in capabilities.py, taking NO model or provider argument at all, so it cannot gate on a name shape. One WebSearch(native=WebSearchTool(max_uses=5), local=duckduckgo_search_tool(max_results=5)). New profile-derived ModelCapabilities.native_web_search read by MEMBERSHIP in supported_native_tools. provider_provenance.capabilities.web_access records "native" | "local" | "off". The duckduckgo group was folded into the agents extra itself so no deployment can install the agents runtime and forget it; uv.lock regenerated. Full suite 9863 passed.

A TRAP THE IMPLEMENTER FOUND THAT MUST NOT BE UNDONE: setting max_uses / blocked_domains / allowed_domains at the CAPABILITY level flips pydantic-ai's _requires_native() to True, and NativeOrLocalTool.get_toolset() then returns None - which SUPPRESSES the local fallback and hard-fails on any provider lacking the native tool. That is the original bug re-created. max_uses therefore rides the NATIVE TOOL INSTANCE, and a test asserts get_toolset() is not None. Do not "harden" the capability by moving those kwargs up a level.

STILL OWED ON THIS TICKET: AC2 asks for verification by a RUN on each configured provider. What exists is the attach path exercised per provider through the runner plus the route read off each real profile - no live model call. A live Bedrock plan-review showing web_access "local" on a signed verdict would close it outright.

PATCHSET 2 pushed to Gerrit 1344, clearing BOTH -1 votes from patchset 1.

--- BLOCK 1: LLM-Review-1 (bugfix-size-attestation) — CLEARED, no LLM spend ---
Not a code finding: 554 non-test lines exceeds the 150-line floor for a bug fix, so the Gerrit
bugfix-size gate demanded a certified plan-review attestation, and the record read
"unsigned; no plan-review attestation record". A recorded REVIEW_RESULT sidecar already existed
and was merely stale, so `rebar sign-review 129e-2d88-cce2-492c` re-signed it from that sidecar
with NO review re-run:
  {"ok": true, "signed": true, "verdict": "PASS",
   "reason": "re-signed the plan-review attestation from the latest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar
              (no LLM review re-run)"}
Signed at d39bc122d756bcd76ef638dfd606b24812bbb349 (= origin/main at push time). Verified the
SIGNATURE event reached the remote: commit 4a0c1358be on origin/tickets, and the local store HEAD
is an ancestor of origin/tickets, so the review bot can see it.

--- BLOCK 2: Verified-1 — DIAGNOSED AND FIXED. It was NOT the stale-base trap. ---
Run 30873144317 failed the SAME way on all four matrix legs (ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 + macos 3.13):
  FAILED tests/unit/test_web_tool_gating.py::test_runner_attaches_web_capability_on_every_provider[bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8]
  FAILED tests/unit/test_web_tool_gating.py::test_runner_unflagged_request_is_byte_identical[bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8]
  2 failed, 9814 passed  — a genuine 2-test failure, not a missing gate script.

ROOT CAUSE — a host-dependent test of MY OWN, not a production defect. Both cases are the
bedrock leg of a provider-parametrized test. Only the Agent class is doubled (via the
`_import_pydantic_ai` seam); the MODEL/PROVIDER is still built for real, and
`build_bedrock_provider` resolves BOTH a region and credentials at construction time. This host
has both in its ambient AWS config, so the tests passed locally; CI has neither, so they failed.
The suite cited earlier (9863 passed) was therefore green only because of ambient host config.

Reproduced locally before fixing, by stripping exactly what CI lacks:
  env -u AWS_DEFAULT_REGION -u AWS_REGION -u AWS_PROFILE HOME=<empty dir> pytest tests/unit/test_web_tool_gating.py
  -> 2 failed, 18 passed — the identical two cases, the identical LLMConfigError.

Both failure arms were then measured separately:
  * no region -> LLMConfigError from build_bedrock_provider's boto3 region pre-check;
  * region pinned but no credentials -> botocore reaches for IMDS and trips the repo's
    network-forbidden fixture ("Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests").
So pinning the region ALONE is insufficient — the first fix attempt proved exactly that by
still failing.

FIX (test-only, 13 lines in tests/unit/test_web_tool_gating.py::_agent_kwargs):
  * region via the LLMConfig FIELD (`bedrock_region_name="us-east-1"`), deliberately NOT via
    REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION — that env var is read only by LLMConfig's env/table factory
    (config.py:578), never by the direct construction this helper does, so a monkeypatched env
    var silently falls through to boto3's ambient resolution and keeps the host-dependence.
    (Measured: the env-var attempt did not change the result.)
  * credentials via botocore's env provider (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    placeholders), which short-circuits the IMDS lookup.
Mirrors the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY placeholder the same helper already sets. No client call is made,
so neither value is used. NO production file changed.

VERIFIED both directions:
  faithful CI sim (no AWS env, empty HOME): 20 passed
  this host (ambient AWS config present):   20 passed
The case is now hermetic instead of passing for the wrong reason.

Per the standing decision, `max_uses`/`blocked_domains`/`allowed_domains` were left on the native
tool instance — hoisting them to the capability level flips pydantic-ai's `_requires_native()` True
and suppresses the local fallback. The guard pinning `get_toolset() is not None` still passes.

--- FULL GATE RUN at 6700cf8ddd, clean tree, judged by exit code only ---
git status --porcelain: EMPTY before the suite run cited below.
PASS: uv lock --check · make lint · make typecheck · make config-check ·
      check_verify_gate_parity · check_comment_hygiene · check_raw_git_writes ·
      check_wall_clock_asserts · check_config_reads · check_docs_index --check ·
      check_readme_quickstart · check_server_manifest · gen_env_registry.py --check ·
      security_pin
Generators (gen_cli_reference / gen_mcp_reference / gen_env_registry) re-run: left the tree clean.
FULL DEFAULT SUITE: 9879 passed, 34 skipped, 0 failed in 471.94s
  (pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 6 --dist worksteal)

compiled_state.description:
# The cutover withdrew a BLOCKING criterion's grounding tool, by prefix match, with no signal

## Context / Problem

Plan-review criterion **T1** (`facet: overlay-priorart`, `exec: AGENT`, `default_posture: **blocking**`)
declares `"web": true` in the packaged routing registry
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`). Its reviewer prompt
(`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T1.md`) instructs the model: *"when the web-search tool is
offered, USE it to ground prior-art claims in real, current sources."* T1 is the bright-line overlay —
it fires on external integration, unfamiliar dependency, security/auth, a novel architectural pattern,
a perf/scalability target, or a migration.

The tool is attached only by this gate (`src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py`,
`_anthropic_web_search_capabilities`):

    if not web or not resolved.startswith("anthropic"):
        return None

**Since the production review bot was cut over to Bedrock [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a], `resolved` is
`bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, which does not start with `anthropic`. So T1 now runs WITHOUT
its grounding tool on every production plan review.** The live chain, each link verified:
`criteria_routing.json` `"web": true` -> `criteria/model.py` `"web": bool(routing_entry.get("web", False))`
-> `plan_review/passes.py` `web=agentic and any(bool(c.get("web")) for c in chunk)` -> `runner.py`
`_anthropic_web_search_capabilities(resolved, web=req.web)` -> the prefix gate above.

## Why this matters

1. **It is a BLOCKING criterion.** T1 can block a plan. It now does so on weaker evidence — codebase
   and model knowledge instead of current sources — for exactly the plans that cross a bright-line.
2. **It is decided by PREFIX SHAPE, not capability.** The epic's standing rule is provider
   qualification by REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP, never prefix matching, with zero exceptions — enforced for the
   capabilities module by an attested guard. This site is the same anti-pattern in a different module,
   and the cutover is what made it bite: the identical MODEL (Claude) reached through a different
   PROVIDER loses a capability because of how its name is spelled.
3. **It is SILENT.** No warning is logged and the signed verdict's `provider_provenance.capabilities`
   records `native_structured_output`, `prompt_cache_style`, `supports_temperature` and
   `supports_thinking` — but nothing about web search. So a reader of the verdict cannot tell that a
   declared grounding tool was withheld. This is the failure shape the epic kept hitting: the guard
   shares the bug's assumption.
4. **It contradicts the epic's own premise.** Epic 061c asserts `first_class = full fidelity`, and
   both Anthropic and Bedrock are first-class. This is a measurable fidelity difference between them
   that no acceptance criterion covers.

**Not a hallucination risk** — and this is the one piece of good news. T1's prompt handles absence
explicitly: *"when it is not available, fall back to codebase and plan-text reasoning ... and do NOT
fabricate web citations."* So the degradation is quiet quality loss, not invented sources.

## OPERATOR DECISION: web access is REQUIRED for T1 regardless of provider or model

This supersedes the branch this ticket was originally filed with. I had written that if Bedrock does
not support Anthropic's server-side `web_search`, then returning `None` is CORRECT and the defect is
merely that it is silent. **That is wrong.** The operator's requirement is that **T1 needs web access
on EVERY provider and model.** A provider that cannot offer it is a capability gap rebar must CLOSE,
not a difference rebar may document.

Two consequences follow, and the second is the harder one:

1. **The prefix gate goes regardless.** `resolved.startswith("anthropic")` cannot decide this, both
   because it is prefix matching (the epic's zero-exceptions rule) and because the answer it computes
   is no longer the question being asked.

2. **Provider-side-only is no longer a sufficient design.** The current implementation is deliberately
   provider-side: `plan_review_T1.md` and `anthropic_model.py` both state the tool is Anthropic's
   SERVER-SIDE `web_search`, "executed provider-side, no homegrown HTTP fetch tool" — an explicit
   decision to avoid rebar owning a fetch tool. If web access must hold for every provider, that
   decision must be REVISITED rather than worked around: where a provider offers a server-side tool,
   prefer it; where it does not, rebar must supply the access some other way. Whatever is chosen, it
   must satisfy the constraint the original design was protecting — the reviewer must not be handed an
   unbounded homegrown HTTP fetch capability without thinking about egress, caching and prompt-injection
   from fetched content. That tradeoff is the real work in this ticket and should not be skipped past.

STILL MEASURE BEDROCK FIRST — the measurement now selects the MECHANISM rather than deciding whether
there is a bug: if Bedrock's Converse API can carry the server-side tool, that is the cheapest correct
path for the current production provider and no rebar-side fetch tool is needed yet. If it cannot,
the rebar-side path is required. Either way T1 ends up with web access.

ALSO REVISIT T1's PROMPT. It currently tells the reviewer the tool "MAY be offered on this run (it is
provider-dependent...)" and to fall back to codebase reasoning when absent. Under this decision that
conditional framing is wrong: web access is a guarantee for T1, so the prompt should assert it rather
than hedge. The graceful-degradation clause protected against fabricated citations and should not be
deleted carelessly — but it must stop describing absence as an expected state.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities`, the prefix gate.
- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — most likely home for a profile-derived `supports_server_web_search`
  capability, alongside the existing `prompt_cache_style` / `native_structured_output` decisions.
- the `provider_provenance.capabilities` payload, so the outcome is observable in a signed verdict.

## Testing

- a test that with a `bedrock:`-qualified Claude model and `web=True`, the outcome matches the MEASURED
  Bedrock capability — and that the decision does not consult the provider-name string. Verify RED by
  reinstating a prefix match.
- a test that the signed verdict's provenance records whether server-side web search was attached, so
  the silent case cannot return. Verify RED by removing the field.
- record the Bedrock measurement itself (a real call with the capability requested) as the evidence for
  whichever branch the fix takes; "not supported" is an acceptable answer, an unmeasured assumption is
  not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] whether Bedrock's Converse API can carry Anthropic's server-side `web_search` is MEASURED and
      recorded, with the call and its outcome. This selects the mechanism; it does not decide whether
      there is a bug.
- [ ] T1 has WEB ACCESS ON EVERY PROVIDER rebar can route it to, including Bedrock — verified by a run
      on each configured provider, not by inspection of the gate condition.
- [ ] the web-access decision no longer consults a provider-name prefix; it derives from the model
      profile / capability registry, consistent with the epic's zero-exceptions rule. The attested
      guard `test_capabilities_module_still_has_no_provider_name_prefix_matching` is NOT weakened.
- [ ] if a rebar-side mechanism is required for any provider, the egress / caching /
      prompt-injection-from-fetched-content tradeoff that the original provider-side-only design was
      protecting is addressed explicitly, not bypassed.
- [ ] a signed verdict's `provider_provenance.capabilities` records that web access WAS attached, so a
      future silent withdrawal is impossible to miss.
- [ ] `plan_review_T1.md` no longer describes web access as provider-dependent or optional, while still
      forbidding fabricated citations.
- [ ] tests pin the above and are each verified RED by mutation, including one that fails if the
      capability is withheld on a `bedrock:`-qualified model.
compiled_state.title: Bedrock cutover silently removed server-side web search from blocking criterion T1, gated by provider-name prefix
